subject: what if rents drop 10 percent
preheader: sensitivity analysis shows how selected input changes affect the model.
headline: A base case is only one modeled scenario.
body: Sensitivity analysis is the practice of asking 'what if I'm wrong?' What if rents drop 10%? What if interest rates rise another point on refinance? What if vacancy doubles? What if insurance jumps 50%?

In a simplified illustration with all other modeled amounts fixed, $400 monthly cash flow at $2,000 rent becomes $200 at $1,800 rent. A further 5% reduction from $1,800 is $90, leaving about $110 — not zero. Real variable expenses may change the result.

An illustrative base case can change materially when rent, vacancy, or the modeled interest rate changes. The point is not that one preset stress case predicts the future; it is to expose which assumption the modeled result depends on most.

A result that remains positive under selected stresses may have more modeled cushion, but it is not automatically a good investment or an approved loan. Choose ranges that fit the property, verify the evidence, and consider risks the grid does not model.

When entitled, TrueCap's released sensitivity grid reruns cash flow, cap rate, cash-on-cash, and DSCR at entered values plus rent −10%/+10%, vacancy +5/−5 percentage points, and interest rate +1/−1 percentage point. The interest-rate row is omitted for an all-cash purchase.
